subject: general
question: Which of the following substances is insoluble in water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalk Powder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium Carbonate is the carbonic salt of calcium (CaCO3).
 
• Calcium Carbonate (also known as chalk), mined as calcite, is the most commonly used filler for PVC.
 
• Calcium Carbonate is insoluble in water because the electrostatic bonds between the carbonate anion and the calcium ion are too strong to be overcome by solvation by water molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**

 
• It is the chemical name for salt.
 
• Sodium is an electrolyte that regulates the amount of water in your body.
 
• Soluble in: Water, Ammonia, Methanol, Glycerol, Formic acid, Propylene glycol, Formamide.

**Lithium Bromide (LiBr)**

 
• It is a lithium salt in which the counterion is bromide.
 
• The anhydrous salt forms cubic crystals are similar to common salt.
 
• It is soluble in water, alcohol, and ether.
 
• It is prepared by the action of hydrobromic acid on lithium hydroxide.

**Magnesium Iodide (MgI2)**

 
• It is typical ionic halides, being highly soluble in water.
